files.document_title: Plaquemines Expansion Project draft Resource Report 1, Figure 1.8-1 Location of Cloud Connector Project, Burns and McDonnell, issued 8/15/2025, accession 20250822-5162, docket PF25-7-000
files.fetch_route: FERC eLibrary download service (curl POST), then pdftoppm at 150 dpi
files.what_it_shows: A 1:1,600,000 statewide map of the full Cloud Connector route in red, from the north end near Monroe in Richland Parish south through Franklin, Catahoula, Concordia, Avoyelles, St. Landry, Pointe Coupee, Iberville, Assumption, Lafourche and Terrebonne parishes to the Plaquemines Expansion terminal in Plaquemines Parish, with mileposts every 10 miles to about 292. A blue North Perryville Extension of about 20 miles is shown at the north end. The route is a 300 mile line.

files.document_title: Exhibit A, May 2026 Cloud Connector Joint Permit Application Narrative, filed by Healthy Gulf and Louisiana Bucket Brigade, accession 20260922-5112, docket CP26-53-000
files.what_it_shows: Text only, with no figures included. It describes the preferred route in words: it starts at Trap Site 2 in Assumption Parish about 2.5 miles northwest of Paincourtville, goes southeast 25 miles to Compressor Station 1 south of Thibodaux, then crosses Lafourche Parish and the Delaune-Walds Levee System to Trap Site 1. It gives 165.1 miles of 48-inch pipe.

searched: The oilandgaswatch record has no attached documents.
FERC eLibrary full text search for the phrase Cloud Connector, which found the Plaquemines Expansion dockets CP26-27-000, CP26-53-000 and PF25-7-000.
Resource Report 1 of the Plaquemines Expansion draft filing, which holds the only public route map found.
A protest filing's Exhibit A, which is the May 2026 joint permit application narrative with no figures.
Web search for the Army Corps of Engineers New Orleans District public notice and Venture Global route maps, which found nothing usable.
notes: The map shows the full route at statewide scale only, which is coarse, but it has mileposts every 10 miles and many named towns and parish outlines for a georeferencer. The length is about 300 miles in the Plaquemines filing, matching the sheet. The permit narrative describes 165.1 miles of 48-inch pipe within the Army Corps of Engineers New Orleans District, so oilandgaswatch's 165 miles is that district portion and not the full line. Detailed alignment figures (Figure Sets 3 and 4 of the permit application) were not found in public filings. The FERC eLibrary page is a JavaScript application, so the URL checker calls it a JavaScript shell. The files were downloaded directly and read. The map's basemap credit mentions OpenStreetMap contributors, but the route itself is Burns and McDonnell's drawing.
